meta.title: Deepfy Health Record
meta.description: Built for your health. Read by your agents. Family health records, checkup tracking, encrypted storage.

hero.mcpPrompt:
Please add "Deepfy Health Record" as an MCP server so you can read (and, after I confirm, write to) my health record.

- Name: deepfy
- Type: remote MCP (Streamable HTTP)
- URL: {url}
- Header: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DEEPFY_TOKEN

I create the token by signing in at {app} and opening Agents (it also offers a full prompt with the token filled in). Replace YOUR_DEEPFY_TOKEN with my token; if I haven't given you one yet, remind me to create one first, then finish the setup.

Add it the way your client supports (CLI command or mcpServers in the config file). Then call list_members to confirm the connection and read deepfy://contract for the data guide and write rules. The token is a password: only put it in the MCP config, never commit it to a git repository or send it anywhere else.
hero.lead1: Give Deepfy your reports, records and daily metrics.
hero.lead2:
You see clear health cards;
your agent gets structured, encrypted data with reminders.

flow.title: From one report to a family health record
flow.lead: Hand reports to your agent and they become a structured record in the cloud; Deepfy then reminds you when rechecks and checkups are due.
flow.s1: PDFs, photos or lab slips. Your agent reads every item, maps it to one dictionary and saves it — reference ranges come from your report.
flow.s2: Everyone's results, history and recheck plans, encrypted in one place. Switch agents and they read the same record; every change is logged and revertible.
flow.s3: Rechecks and annual checkups are scheduled for you, with an email 7 days before and on the day. Mark items Done, or Skipped when your doctor says so.
flow.mailPause: Too many? Pause with one click

agents.title: Works with the assistants you already use
agents.lead: Over MCP, agents like Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grokbot, WorkBuddy and Hermes Agent can read your health record and, with your confirmation, log symptoms, update your profile, import reports and save their analysis.
agents.note: MCP is live: sign in, create a token under Agents and send the generated prompt to your agent — it sets itself up. Each token can be read-only or allowed to write, and every agent write can be undone in one click.

security.title: Your health data belongs to you
security.lead: We use it only to serve you. Never sold, never used for ads.
security.c1: Profiles, records, reports and attachments are stored with AES-256-GCM encryption.
security.c2: Each account has its own data key, wrapped by a separately kept master key. Health content in backups stays encrypted.
security.c3: This is server-side encryption, not end-to-end: to display and analyze your data, the server decrypts it in memory.
security.c4: Export everything in one click; deleting your account removes records and attachments.

family.title: One account for the whole family
family.lead: Separate records for parents, partners and kids — markers, reminders and medications never mix.

final.title: Start with your next checkup report
final.lead: Free to use for now. Hand your report to your agent and it will enter it for you.

docs.title: Get started with Deepfy
docs.lead: Set up your family's health record in a few minutes, then connect it to the AI assistant you already use.

steps.d: On the sign-in page, continue with Google or your email. The first time, accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy; with email, also set a password and enter the code we send. That creates your account, and after that you just sign in.
Give each person a nickname and their relation to you. If you don't know a birth date, an approximate age is fine.

Hand your checkup or lab report to a connected agent (see Connect an agent below) and it will enter it item by item. There's no report entry form on the web yet; from the top of Overview you can log notes and daily readings (symptoms, photos, weight, blood pressure…).
Overview sums up what's out of range and what to recheck next; Markers shows how each item changes over time.

agents.title: Connect an agent (MCP)
agents.lead: Deepfy runs a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Once connected, agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Grokbot can read your health record and, with your permission, record and organize it.

steps.d: Open Agents in the app and create a token, read-only or with write access. Use one token per agent so you can see usage and revoke each separately; the free plan allows 3.
The page generates a prompt that includes the token. Send it to your agent and it sets itself up — or configure it by hand with the examples below.
Ask your agent to call list_members. If it lists your family, you're connected.

agents.promptHint: Send this to your agent (no token included). It will ask you to create a token, then finish the setup itself.
agents.snippetHint: Replace {token} with your token. Most other agents accept the generic "HTTP + custom header" format (Gemini CLI uses the httpUrl field).
agents.canTitle: What a connected agent can do
can: Read profiles, checkup and lab results, marker trends and the recheck plan.
Import reports, log symptoms and notes, update profiles and schedule rechecks (needs a write token).
Record medication and supplements, read strength and use-by dates from package photos, and suggest common supplements from the profile (suggestions take effect only after you agree).
Every write is listed under Agents and can be reverted in one click.
A token works like a password: keep it only in your agent's MCP config, never commit it to git, and revoke it when you stop using it. Data your agent reads is sent to its model provider.

items.d: The app home lists everyone with their number of out-of-range items. Switch people from the name next to the logo.
One person's health summary: out-of-range markers, findings, and the rechecks and checkups coming up next. Log notes and daily readings right from the top.
Browse every test by category and open one to see past values against the reference range.
The full history of checkups, lab tests, medical records and log entries. Reports are entered by your agent; log entries can include photos.
Out-of-range items go into a recheck plan: mark them Done, or Skipped when your doctor says no need. We email you before they're due; pause under Reminders in the avatar menu.

Keep track of medication and supplements: what to take today, precautions and use-by dates are all on this page. Add them yourself, or send a prescription or package photo to your agent. Your agent can suggest common supplements from the profile; those suggestions come from your own agent, not a doctor. Medication is only recorded as prescribed; follow your doctor on starting, stopping or changing a dose.
Basic details, medical history and allergies. Agents take these into account.
See your usage, export everything (ZIP with attachments), or delete your account.
Sign in and choose Feedback in the avatar menu — a few lines is enough. Your sign-in email is attached so we can reply. We read every one.

privacy.title: Data & privacy
items: Records, reports and attachments are encrypted on the server (AES-256-GCM) with a separate key per account. This is server-side encryption, not end-to-end.
Export everything from Settings at any time; deleting your account deletes the data and attachments too.
Every account is free for now, with up to 6 family members, 500 MB of attachments and 3 agent tokens — see the Terms.
All analysis is for reference only and is not a substitute for medical advice.

scenes.title: Ask your agent
scenes.lead: It has read your whole family's record, so it can answer specifics: read results, give advice, plan rechecks, log symptoms.
scenes.note: Example people are fictional; agent advice is for reference only and is not a substitute for medical advice.

diet.q: Based on my checkup, what should I watch with diet and exercise lately?
diet.a: Focus on triglycerides at 2.6 (high) and sitting too much. Cut sugary drinks to the occasional one; aim for 150 minutes of brisk walking a week plus 2 strength sessions. We'll see the effect at the January recheck.

trip.q: I'm hiking up to 4,000 m next month. Anything I should know given my health?
trip.a: Your blood pressure and ECG are normal, but they can't tell you your altitude risk on their own — ascent rate, sleeping altitude and any past altitude sickness matter too. I've put together notes for your itinerary: sleep no more than 500 m higher each day, your low-normal hemoglobin, and 3 questions to ask your doctor before you go.

family.q: When is Mom's next recheck, and what for?
family.a: Lipids on 20 Nov — her last LDL was 3.9, high. With her hypertension, she hasn't had a urine microalbumin test yet. Shall I add it to her plan?

doctor.q: I'm seeing a cardiologist tomorrow. Summarize what to show them.
doctor.a: One page: LDL 3.2 → 3.9 over 3 years, a 2026 ECG noting flat T waves, no current medication. You could ask whether a carotid ultrasound is worth doing.

log.q: Bit of a headache today, BP 138/92 — log it for me.
log.a: Logged for today. Systolic has been over 135 3 times in two weeks — measure morning and evening for 7 days, then ask me for a summary.

report.q: Here's this year's checkup report (38-page PDF).
report.a: All 101 items are in, 4 need attention. The ALT recheck is set for 15 Jan, and you'll get an email before it's due.

member.conditionPrompt:
Please use the Deepfy MCP server to read my health record (member "{name}", id: {id}) and do a health review of "{condition}":

1. First ask me: when and how it was found (checkup / ultrasound / blood test), whether I have a report or numbers; my recent diet, alcohol, exercise, sleep and weight changes; any related discomfort.
2. Record the details I confirm: reports with add_record (preview first), habits with update_profile, discomfort with add_log.
3. Research it against my data and write a health plan with update_care_plan: where I stand, diet and lifestyle changes, markers to watch ({codes}) and when to recheck, and when to see a doctor; write analysis for abnormal markers with save_indicator_note.

Confirm with me before every write.

settings.title: Settings
settings.securityText: All traffic uses HTTPS. Profiles, records, reports and attachments are stored with AES-256-GCM encryption, one key per account. They're decrypted on the server only when you view them or use analysis. This is not end-to-end encryption.
settings.tokensHint: Let your agent (Claude Code, Codex, Grokbot…) read your health record over MCP and, with your confirmation, record and organize it. Create an access token and send the generated prompt to your agent — it will set itself up. You can copy the setup again here any time. Use one token per agent so you can see usage and revoke each separately. Data your agent reads is sent to its model provider; revoke the token when you no longer use it.

template.title: Checkup suggestions
template.none: All routine items are up to date.
template.disclaimer: Based on routine checkups for working adults and your records. For reference only — follow your doctor's advice.

body.name: Body measures
body.why: Weight, BMI and waist are the first signals of metabolic risk

bp.name: Blood pressure
bp.why: Often silent early on — check regularly if you sit a lot or sleep late

cbc.name: Complete blood count
cbc.why: Baseline screen for anemia, infection and blood issues

liver.name: Liver function
liver.why: Alcohol, greasy takeaway food and fatty liver are common

glucose.name: Blood glucose
glucose.why: Fasting glucose and HbA1c for glucose metabolism

thyroid.name: Thyroid function
thyroid.why: Worth checking with fatigue, palpitations, mood or weight changes

vitd.name: Vitamin D
vitd.why: Often low for indoor workers with little sun

ecg.name: ECG
ecg.why: Baseline heart rhythm and ischemia check

ultrasound.name: Abdominal ultrasound
ultrasound.why: Liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys — fatty liver is common

chest.name: Chest X-ray / CT
chest.why: Baseline lung screen, more important for smokers

eye.name: Eye exam
eye.why: Long screen hours: vision, eye pressure, fundus

spine.name: Neck & back
spine.why: Assess if desk work causes neck, shoulder or back pain

breast.name: Breast exam
breast.why: Yearly breast ultrasound for women over 30

cervix.name: Cervical screening
cervix.why: Pap / HPV at the interval your doctor advises

psa.name: PSA
psa.why: Prostate screening from 50 — discuss with your doctor
